brief.purpose: Review margin recovery and account retention in a fictional distributor slice.
questions: Where does growth conceal weaker contribution?
Which account declines have supporting service evidence?
constraints: All business details are fictional; no real company research.

claims.statement: The fictional organization has no public product taxonomy.
claims.gap: Use explicitly synthetic dimensions for integration testing.

blueprint.slice: Fictional B2B components sales across two territories and three product families.
blueprint.economic_policy: Decimal money; gross profit = revenue minus product cost; contribution further subtracts allocated fulfillment and program costs. Missing cost blocks profitability. Refunds and recovery are applied once. No realized benefit is claimed.
blueprint.overlap_policy: Store affected records; compare combined state to baseline and report interaction residual separately.

relationships.temporal_rule: Purchaser must belong to the order account on order date.
relationships.aggregation_rule: Sum order-line revenue once by customer; never multiply by purchaser count.

facts.grain: One product on an order line
facts.allocation_policy: Allocate shipment costs once to lines; allocations reconcile to shipment totals.

stories.title: Growth with weaker contribution
stories.mechanism: Increase effective supplier costs, shift demand toward lower-margin SKUs, and raise expedite usage.
stories.scope: Selected product families; overlap with affected accounts.
stories.timing: Events begin 2025-07-01; service precedes account reduction by 30 days.
stories.effect_bounds: Proposed: sales change +2% to +12%; contribution change -5% to -25%.
operational_evidence: Orders joined to product and customer dimensions
Effective costs and allocated shipment costs
alternatives: Seasonality or changes in purchase mix
prohibited_claims: Competitor loss or definitive churn without evidence
stories.synthetic_rationale: Mechanism test only; not inspired by an actual news event.

stories.title: Two declining accounts, one partial explanation
stories.mechanism: Reduce purchasing at two accounts; preceding service disruption is observable for only one.
stories.scope: Two commercial accounts, aggregating all their purchasers.
stories.comparison_basis: Account plan and prior year; no causal interpretation of those gaps.
stories.timing: Events begin 2025-07-01; service precedes account reduction by 30 days.
stories.effect_bounds: Proposed: each affected account sales -15% to -35%; unaffected cohort -5% to +10%.
operational_evidence: Orders joined to product and customer dimensions
Effective costs and allocated shipment costs
alternatives: Seasonality or changes in purchase mix
prohibited_claims: Competitor loss or definitive churn without evidence
stories.synthetic_rationale: Mechanism test only; not inspired by an actual news event.
